title: Arc Press
pages: Craft the controller from two Porcelain Insulators in the top corners (fire Green Porcelain Insulators in the Clinker Oven; they keep the discharge electrode from arcing into the frame, so bare chains or unfired green insulators are refused), four copper ingots, one conductive crystal (electrolyze purified salts) and two Broach Press-made broached pins in the bottom corners. Place a raw copper block directly beneath it, a redstone torch directly above it, and chains on all four horizontal sides. At each of the four diagonal corners, place a copper block at controller height and a lightning rod on top: these posts collect the discharge around the chain-suspended electrode. Any missing post, tip, side, cap or base stops operation. Use the Structure Projector on the controller to see each layer. Material update: crafting slot 2 (row-major 3x3) now requires an iridium ingot via forge:ingots/iridium; all existing progression gates remain required.

Right-click the formed controller with feedstock from a loaded arc_discharge recipe to load it into the stock buffer; nothing comes out instantly. Each batch then runs for the recipe's duration and draws its FE every tick: 80 ticks at 32 FE/t by default, 160 ticks at 48 FE/t for the Fused Steel Plate weld. Without FE the batch stalls with status no_power and keeps its progress. Frame parts cover every controller face, so feed FE from a cable or generator into a Stock Hatch that replaces one of them; the controller holds 16,000 FE. Right-click with an empty hand to collect the product. Hand use and automation share one buffer, the same recipes and the same time and power.

It runs 20 exclusive datapack arc_discharge recipes. Nineteen arc-salvage scrap at a lossy ratio. Compass, iron trapdoor and heavy pressure plate return iron ingots; clock and light plate return gold; lightning rod and spyglass return copper; dropper, dispenser and piston return their redstone. The rest yield reusable stock: anvil to 2 iron blocks, cauldron to 12 iron bars, bucket to a heavy pressure plate, hopper to its chest, minecart to 8 rails, 2 iron doors to a trapdoor, sticky piston to its slime ball, shears to a chain, 2 tripwire hooks to 9 iron nuggets. The twentieth arc-welds two Sealed Steel Plates (each pressed from one carburized steel billet) into a single laminated Fused Steel Plate; the arc melts the seam so both sheets solidify as one stiffer platen. With JEI installed, search the Arc Press controller for the Arc Discharge category; it shows loaded recipes, exact batch counts and formation requirements.

A Fused Steel Plate replaces the Resonance Infuser's last bottom-left plain sealed steel plate, alongside the Wound Coil, the Charged Capacitor, the Magnetized Core, the conductive crystal, one vitrified amethyst, a Resonant Rune, the harmonic lens and an electrolyzer. This is the fifth required t4 apparatus; no plain ingredient remains in that craft.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded arc discharge recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch per recipe duration while paying the recipe's FE each tick, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress, stored FE and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer. Hatches also relay Forge Energy into this powered controller, so a cable or generator touching a hatch keeps it running.
